Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort on the 80th Independence Day, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi announced a series of initiatives and targets covering Artificial Intelligence, education, sports, Civil Defence, semiconductor manufacturing, nuclear energy and women-led development.
Key announcements from the Prime Minister’s address include:
1. AI Skilling for One Crore Youth: The Prime Minister announced that one crore youth would be trained in AI skills over the next one year. Referring to the rapid expansion of Artificial Intelligence, he said the initiative would help equip India’s youth with the capability to lead in the world of AI.
2. Free Online Coaching for Various Examinations: The Prime Minister announced free online coaching for youth preparing for various examinations. Referring to the financial burden of coaching classes on poor and middle-class families, he said Digital Public Infrastructure, available talent and teachers would be brought together to create a complete network for providing free coaching to the country’s youth.
3. Nationwide Sports Talent Hunt for Children Aged 5-15 Years: The Prime Minister announced a talent hunt campaign across villages, cities and schools to identify sporting talent among children between five and 15 years of age. The identified children would be provided specialised training to develop them into players capable of representing the country. Referring to Olympic disciplines in which India currently does not participate or qualify, the Prime Minister said greater emphasis would be placed on building capabilities in such sports.
4. Vibrant Civil Defence Network for Modern Challenges: Highlighting the changing nature of warfare, the Prime Minister announced that a vibrant Civil Defence network would be created in the country. He said that warfare was no longer necessarily confined to borders and could also affect refineries, the banking sector, data centres, factories and other infrastructure. The Prime Minister said that Civil Defence arrangements developed in accordance with the wars of the previous century had become outdated. Citizens would therefore be familiarised with modern systems, and a large voluntary Civil Defence force capable of dealing with modern challenges would be developed.

Union Minister Shri Jual Oram and Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, Jointly Release National Framework and Operational Guidelines for Strengthening of ITDAs and ITDPs
articles.full_content:
Twin publications, translate a nationwide consultative exercise covering 217 ITDAs/ITDPs across 19 States/UTs into an actionable reform roadmap for last-mile tribal development delivery
The Union Minister for Tribal Affairs, Shri Jual Oram, and Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, today jointly released two important publications of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs — the “ National Framework for Strengthening of ITDAs and ITDPs ” and the “ Operational Guidelines for Strengthening of ITDAs and ITDPs. ” The two documents mark the culmination of a comprehensive, consultative and evidence-based national exercise aimed at strengthening Integrated Tribal Development Agencies and Projects (ITDAs/ITDPs), the principal field-level institutions driving tribal development across the country.
The publications were released in the presence of Smt. Ranjana Chopra, Secretary, Tribal Affairs, Shri Manish Thakur, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, and other senior officers of the Ministry.
Speaking on the occasion, the Minister noted that ITDAs/ITDPs have historically served as a critical bridge between government programmes and tribal communities, and that their role has grown even more significant with the scale of interventions under the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) and PM-JANMAN.
Dr. Balasubramaniam noted that the principles of ranking, real-time data-driven monitoring and convergence that delivered saturation of outcomes in under-developed districts and blocks now stand embedded in the ITDA/ITDP reform architecture. He observed that evidence-based administrative attention can transform lagging regions, these publications seek to replicate that model within the tribal development ecosystem, using ITDAs as the delivery vehicle for saturation of entitlements at the last mile.
The exercise was undertaken under the overall guidance and vision of Secretary, Tribal Affairs, Smt. Ranjana Chopra, whose emphasis on evidence-based, field-driven institutional reform shaped the design of the entire consultative process. Smt. Chopra’s consistent direction to move beyond a one-size-fits-all approach and build context-specific, accountable
field institutions provided the strategic anchor for the Ministry’s roadmap for strengthening ITDAs and ITDPs across the country.
The Ministry had initiated this exercise in April 2026, covering 214 ITDAs/ITDPs across 17 States/UTs, through a standardised assessment involving Project Officers, State Tribal Welfare Departments and Tribal Research Institutes. Designed as a bottom-up, consultative exercise rather than a desk-based study, it included State-level workshops, field visits and direct consultations, allowing ground-level challenges and successful practices to shape the national roadmap. The exercise culminated in the Evidence-Weighted ITDA Diagnostic Scoring Framework, assessing institutions across 15 parameters spanning five institutional domains.

PM Vishwakarma Beneficiaries Invited as ‘Special Guests’ to Witness 80th Independence Day Ceremony at Red Fort, Delhi
articles.full_content:
100 beneficiaries from Delhi-NCR to attend the Celebration
The Government of India has invited 100 beneficiaries of PM Vishwakarma from the Delhi-NCR region as ‘Special Guests’ to witness the 80th Independence Day Ceremony at the Red Fort, Delhi, on 15th August, 2026. The beneficiaries will attend the national celebration along with their spouse/companion.
The Special Guests also include women artisans from various traditional trades, reflecting the scheme’s contribution towards women’s economic empowerment, greater participation in livelihoods and strengthening the role of women in preserving India’s rich artisanal and cultural heritage.
Recognition and Appreciation of Beneficiaries- As part of their participation, the PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries will also be presented with souvenirs as a token of recognition and appreciation, followed by an interaction with officials of the Ministry of MSME on 14 August 2026 at the Indian Institute of Public Administration, Delhi, recognising their contribution to India’s traditional crafts and cultural heritage.
About PM Vishwakarma Scheme-
PM Vishwakarma is one of the flagship initiatives of the Government of India aimed at providing comprehensive support to artisans and craftspeople engaged in traditional trades. The scheme provides assistance through skill upgradation, modern tools, financial support, digital enablement and market linkages, with the objective of promoting the socio-economic empowerment of artisans, strengthening traditional crafts and ensuring sustainable livelihoods. Under the scheme, 30 lakh traditional artisans and craftspeople have been registered.
Celebrating the Contribution of India’s Traditional Artisans & Craftspeople
The invited beneficiaries represent the 18 traditional trades covered under PM Vishwakarma, including Tailor, Carpenter, Goldsmith, Blacksmith, Locksmith, among others. The beneficiaries invited have availed various benefits under the scheme, including registration, Basic Skill Training and provision of toolkits, along with other support benefits available under the scheme.
The participation of PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries in the Independence Day celebration is recognition of the invaluable contribution of traditional artisans and craftspeople to India’s rich cultural heritage. Their presence at the Red Fort will provide them an opportunity to witness the grandeur of the 80th Independence Day and to be a part of this historic national celebration.

articles.title: Software Technology Parks Strengthen India’s IT Export Ecosystem and Ease of Doing Business
articles.full_content:
STP Units Record over ₹7.73 Lakh Crore in Exports in FY 2025-26
The Government of India has launched several initiatives and programs to support the expansion of the IT sector and is constantly working to promote the sector throughout the country. The Software Technology Park (STP) is one such important scheme in this effort.
STP Scheme is a 100% export-oriented scheme to promote software and IT-enabled services (IT/ITeS) exports from India and STPI has been providing Statutory Services on a single-window Clearance System under STP Scheme.

STPI adheres to the prescribed timelines for approvals and delivery of services under the STP Scheme, as outlined in its Citizen’s Charter available at https://stpi.in/en/citizens-charter .
Measures taken by the Software technology Parks of India (STPI) to streamline approvals and improve ease of doing business for STP units are as follows:
• Automation of Statutory Services: For providing seamless services to the IT exporters, statutory services including SOFTEX filling, its approval and final intimation to them has been automated. This has ensured speedy delivery of services to the satisfaction of the IT industry.
• Integration with RBI’s Export Data Processing and Monitoring System (EDPMS) System for IT exporters: STPI’s online system for IT exporters has been integrated with the Reserve Bank of India’s EDPMS for sharing of export data. This integration has enabled seamless electronic transmission of export declaration data to RBI in near real time. This has facilitated faster exchange of export data, enhanced accuracy and transparency, reduced manual intervention, improved monitoring of export transactions, and streamlined regulatory compliance for IT/ITeS exporters.
• Simplification of Import Procedures: The earlier practice of case-to-case import permissions has been replaced with blanket import permissions for the financial year concerned.
• Self-Declaration for Domestic Tariff Area (DTA) Sales: The requirement for prior DTA permissions for STPI-registered units has been replaced with a submission of self-declaration (except for advance DTA sales in first year of operation).
This information was given by Union Minister of Electronics and IT Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw in Lok Sabha on 12.08.2026
Vinod Kumar / Kanishk Sharma

articles.title: FutureSkills PRIME Strengthens India’s Future Ready Digital Workforce Through Skilling in Emerging Technologies
articles.full_content:
Over 34 Lakh Candidates Registered on FutureSkills PRIME Portal; 13 Lakh+ Candidates Certified
Under the visionary leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister, the Government of India is preparing a future-ready workforce. These skills are required in an ecosystem of cutting-edge technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Big Data Analytics, Cyber Security, Internet of Things (IoT), Semiconductors, Cloud Computing, etc across key sectors.
India is a skills capital in IT and known for its strong talent pipeline and skilled workforce, with its IT sector globally recognised for high-quality talent. As per global assessments such as the Stanford AI Index, India ranks among the leading nations in AI adoption, preparedness and ecosystem vibrancy. India also accounts for around 20% of the global semiconductor design workforce, reflecting its emphasis on skilling and talent development. With the rapid adoption of digital technologies across sectors, developing a digitally skilled workforce has become critical for sustaining this growth.
The Government accords priority to digital skilling and capacity building of youth across the country, including those from North Eastern and Himalayan region. Towards this objective, various Ministries and Departments in partnership with industry and with active contribution from academia and R&D institutions are implementing flagship programmes to promote digital literacy, employability and skills in emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Cyber Security, Data Analytics, Drone Technology, Cloud Computing and Semiconductor Design.
Digital India Programme:
As part of the same strategy, the Government of India launched the Digital India Programme in July, 2015 and has been taking steps to ensure that we continue to retain our advantage in IT skills and is promoting skilling in emerging technologies through various initiatives including FutureSkills PRIME programme, so that digital technologies improve the life of every citizen, expand India’s digital economy and create investment and employment opportunities in India. These programmes have enabled large-scale participation of youth and professionals across the country. The outreach model is not only implemented through the FutureSkills PRIME portal but is also supported by the resource centres of C-DAC and NIELIT.
FutureSkills PRIME Programme:
Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology has initiated a programme titled “FutureSkills PRIME” (FSP), jointly with NASSCOM (National Association of Software and Services Companies.) for skilling/ re-skilling/ up-skilling of candidates in new/emerging technologies, aimed at making India a cutting-edge digital talent nation. The FutureSkills PRIME offers industry aligned courses. The platform is an agile model that allows continuous updation of skilling courses in sync with the skill demand.

EPFO REGIONAL OFFICE, MYSURU LAUNCHES “EMPLOYEES’ ENROLMENT CAMPAIGN (EEC) 2026” TO EXPAND SOCIAL SECURITY COVERAGE
articles.full_content:
The Employees' Provident Fund Organization (EPFO), Regional Office, Mysuru, has formally launched the Employees' Enrolment Campaign (EEC), 2026. This special one-time compliance facilitation drive aims to extend statutory social security coverage to eligible employees while encouraging voluntary compliance among employers across the region. The initiative will remain active for a limited period until October 31, 2026.
Under this campaign, employers are enabled to voluntarily enroll eligible employees, who remained outside EPF coverage between April 1, 2009, and March 31, 2026, thereby extending statutory social security benefits while promoting voluntary compliance under the EPF & MP Act. To facilitate smooth participation, the campaign offers significant compliance relief to employers. Where the employee's share of the EPF contribution was not deducted from wages, the same shall be completely waived, requiring employers to remit only the employer's share of contribution alongside applicable interest, administrative charges, and a nominal damage fee of ₹100. Overall, the initiative seeks to expand social security coverage and foster formal employment in the region.
To participate, employers are required to complete the enrolment process digitally through the EPFO Employer Portal using the dedicated EEC-2026 module. The streamlined online process includes submitting a digital declaration, generating Universal Account Numbers (UAN) via Face Authentication technology, filing the Electronic Challan cum Return (ECR), and completing the digital submission of all required declarations.
Highlighting the scope and significance of the campaign, the Regional Provident Fund Commissioner-I, Mysuru, stated that the Employees' Enrolment Campaign provides employers with a unique opportunity to regularize eligible employees while extending essential provident fund, pension, and insurance benefits to them. The Commissioner urged all eligible establishments across the region to avail themselves of the scheme before the final deadline of October 31, 2026.
To ensure seamless implementation and assist establishments in completing the enrolment process, EPFO Mysuru has been actively conducting awareness programmes, employer outreach meetings, and stakeholder interactions throughout the region. Employers seeking further information or assistance are encouraged to visit the official EPFO Employer Portal or directly contact the EPFO Regional Office in Mysuru.

This special one-time compliance facilitation drive aims to extend statutory social security coverage to eligible employees while encouraging voluntary compliance among employers across the region. The initiative will remain active for a limited period until October 31, 2026.

Colourful coral display sparks curiosity, offers insights on climate adaptation research
articles.full_content:
Indication of both resilience and vulnerability to climate stress, says CMFRI
Kochi: In an intriguing spectacle of marine life, a natural coral assemblage in tricolour beneath the sea has sparked curiosity and offered critical insights on climate adaptation research.
The underwater image captured during a marine mammal survey by the ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI) from Minicoy, Lakshadweep shows two coral colonies appearing in tricolour—orange, white and green— come together naturally.
The species were identified as Lobophyllia corymbose with its vibrant orange colour, and Lobophyllia radians in white and green colours.
Captured by CMFRI Research Scholar Alvin Anto, the underwater image provides valuable insights on the contrasting response of corals to environmental stress. While one L. radians colony underwent bleaching after losing its symbiotic algae, its neighbouring colony remains healthy despite growing in close proximity.
Resilience and Vulnerability “Though this assemblage is a symbol of India's rich marine biodiversity, it also carries an urgent message about ocean health. It tells the stark story of resilience and vulnerability to climate stress. While one colony of coral species bleached due to rising sea temperatures, its direct neighbour of the same species remains healthy and green. This variation in thermal stress tolerance offers crucial insights for the ongoing reef restoration and climate adaptation research”, said CMFRI Director Dr Grinson George.
Reef Restoration Emphasising the urgent need to tackle these climate impacts, he highlighted measures being taken up by the CMFRI towards coral reef restoration. “With the support from the Government of India, CMFRI is on a mission to rapidly scale up the deployment of Artificial Reefs along coastal waters to revive degraded habitats, enhance coastal biodiversity, and support the livelihoods of artisanal fishers”, he added.
Simultaneously, efforts are underway to replenish depleted wild stocks of ecologically and economically vital marine species through marine fish breeding, seed production, and sea ranching programmes, Dr George said. Restoring natural habitats through artificial reefs is expected to support marine ecosystems and build a robust climate resilient marine ecosystem, he said, adding that this coral assemblage serves as a reminder to safeguard the fragile coral ecosystems in a warming world.

The species were identified as Lobophyllia corymbose with its vibrant orange colour, and Lobophyllia radians in white and green colours.

Jal Jeevan Mission Clocks Seven Years of Rural Transformation: Rural Drinking Water Tap Coverage Surges from 16.7% to Over 82%
articles.full_content:
Over 2 Lakh Villages, Now ‘Har Ghar Jal’ Certified Focus under JJM 2.0 shifts towards service delivery, source sustainability, community ownership and long-term functionality
As the nation prepares to celebrate the 80 th Independence Day, Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) , the flagship rural drinking water programme of the Government of India, is set to complete seven years of transformative progress in improving the lives of rural households across the country. Launched by Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 15 August 2019, Jal Jeevan Mission aims to provide every rural household with safe and adequate drinking water through a Functional Household Tap Connection (FHTC) on a regular and long-term basis.
At the time of the launch of the Mission, only 3.23 crore rural households, representing about 16.72% of rural households in the country, had tap water connections. Today more than 15.91 crore rural households have tap water supply in their homes, accounting for 82.24% of all rural households. Since the launch of the Mission, over 12.68 crore additional rural households have been provided with tap water connections, significantly improving access to safe drinking water across rural India.
In a major milestone, a total of 188 districts, 1,090 blocks, 1.01 lakh Gram Panchayats and 2.04 lakh villages have been certified as Har Ghar Jal (HGJ) (State-wise details of HGJ Gram Panchayats and Villages at Annex below) , 9.34 lakh (90.86%) schools and 9.73 lakh (86.21%) Anganwadi centres have drinking water tap connections, reflecting the scale and reach of the Mission. The same can be publicly viewed real-time on the Jal Jeevan Mission- Integrated Management Information System (JJM-IMIS) portal https://ejalshakti.gov.in/jjmreport/JJMIndia.aspx
Rural drinking water supply has been a national development priority since Independence. Over the decades, successive initiatives including the National Water Supply Programme (1954), Accelerated Rural Water Supply Programme (1972-73), National Drinking Water Mission (1986), Swajaldhara (2002) and the National Rural Drinking Water Programme (NRDWP) contributed significantly to expanding access to safe drinking water in rural areas. These programmes laid the foundation for strengthening rural water infrastructure and addressing water quality and sustainability challenges. Building upon these efforts, Jal Jeevan Mission marked a paradigm shift from habitation-level coverage to service delivery at the household level through Functional Household Tap Connections, with a focus on adequate quantity (55 lpcd.) of prescribed quality (BIS:10500) on regular and long-term basis at affordable service delivery charges leading to improvement in living standards of rural communities.

articles.title: MSDE convenes India-Japan Stakeholder Consultation to strengthen skilling and workforce pathways between the two countries
articles.full_content:
Consultation focuses on ESDP, Japanese language training, employer linkages and industry-led skilling
The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India, convened the India-Japan Stakeholder Consultation on Skill Development in New Delhi today, bringing together representative from Ministry of External Affairs, State Governments and Sending Organizations, along with Japanese government representatives, Japanese industry representatives, recruitment agents, training partners and other key stakeholders, to strengthen cooperation on skill development and workforce mobility between India and Japan.
The consultation focused on taking forward the Action Plan for India-Japan Human Resource Exchange and Cooperation, jointly released during the 15th India-Japan Annual Summit in 2025. Discussions centred on preparing Indian youth for employment opportunities in Japan through industry-relevant training, Japanese language and cultural preparation, recognised assessments, stronger employer engagement and closer coordination among institutions in both countries.
The consultation was addressed by Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Government of India; H.E. Mr. Ono Keiichi, Ambassador of Japan to India; Ms. Gina Uika, Joint Secretary, Emigration Policy & Welfare (EP&W) Division, Ministry of External Affairs; Ms. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, MSDE; Shri Niranjan Kumar Sudhanshu, Additional Secretary, MSDE; and Shri Arun Kumar Pillai, CEO, National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC). Representatives from Zenken Corporation, Sompo Care, Fourth Valley, Konoike Group and Toyota Kirloskar were also present at the consultation. The programme also featured an audio-visual presentation highlighting the experiences of Indian candidates trained and employed in Japan, showcasing the tangible outcomes of existing cooperation frameworks.
Speaking at the consultation, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (I/C) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Govt of India, said, “India’s young people must be enabled to access global opportunities with the right skills, confidence and preparation, adding that the focus is not only on creating overseas employment pathways but on ensuring that every candidate is equipped with relevant technical skills, language ability and workplace understanding. He noted that the partnership with Japan offers an opportunity to build structured pathways with strong industry participation, and said the discussions would help translate intent into clear action for expanding opportunities for Indian youth.”

articles.title: NITI Aayog releases report on India’s Services Sector: Insights on Regulatory Regime in Professional Services
articles.full_content:
Shri Ashok Kumar Lahiri, Vice Chairman, NITI Aayog, launched the third report under the Services Thematic Series at the forum of the High-Powered ‘Education to Employment and Enterprise’ Standing Committee, in the presence of Smt. Nidhi Chhibber, CEO, NITI Aayog, and Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MOSPI, on 10th August 2026. The launch was attended by senior officers from the Ministries/Departments, State Governments, Industry Associations, and Experts/Academia, who are members of the High-Powered Committee.
The report, “ India’s Services Sector: Insights on Regulatory Regime in Professional Services ”, presents a unique factual assessment of India’s regulatory framework in professional services and benchmarks it against select foreign jurisdictions. Drawing on extensive stakeholder consultations, it also identifies key challenges and outlines a way forward to strengthen the sector and unlock the full potential of India’s professional workforce.
Professional services is a key sub-sector in the services economy, accounting for nearly a quarter of India’s total services exports. As high-value, knowledge-intensive activities, they enable efficient delivery of downstream services, support job creation and remittance inflows, and form the backbone of the services value chain. Understanding the regulatory ecosystem governing these services is therefore critical to unlocking further growth.
The report adopts a balanced approach and provides sector-specific insights, alongside a four-pronged strategy to enhance the efficiency and output of professional services: harnessing emerging trends to transform professional services; elevate professional services within the services value chain; adoption of best practices in professional services, and continuous professional development for professionals.
As India approaches its demographic peak, professional services oﬀer significant opportunities for high-skilled employment, entrepreneurship and innovation. A well-designed regulatory ecosystem can further strengthen service exports, cross-border mobility of professionals and the ease of doing business.
The report provides an indicative pathway for future policy dialogue and deeper examination of the regulatory foundations of professional services. As India advances towards Viksit Bharat @2047, such eﬀorts will be integral to building a globally competitive, inclusive and future-ready services sector.
Read the full report: https://www.niti.gov.in/sites/default/files/2026-08/India-Services-Sector-Insights-on-Regulatory-Regime-in-Professional-Services.pdf

Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MOSPI, on 10th August 2026. The launch was attended by senior officers from the Ministries/Departments, State Governments, Industry Associations, and Experts/Academia, who are members of the High-Powered Committee.

articles.full_content:
Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman highlights the scheme’s role in bridging the gap between classroom learning and industry expectations 86 interns from 24 partner companies participated in the event
Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman, Union Minister of Finance and Corporate Affairs, interacted with interns of the Prime Minister Internship Scheme (PMIS) at New Delhi. The interaction saw participation from 86 interns representing over 24 leading partner companies under PMIS.
Hon’ble Minister interacted with the interns about their experiences, aspirations, and journeys under PMIS. She also spoke with them on what motivated them to participate in the scheme, the learning and skills they gained during their internships, and their future goals.
Several interns who excelled during their internships have been offered full-time roles by their respective companies. The Hon’ble Minister noted that PMIS was designed after extensive consultations with industry, as employers expect fresh graduates to be workplace-ready while many young graduates require practical exposure to meet those expectations. She said the scheme is helping bridge this gap by providing young people with hands-on industry experience.
Speaking to the interns, the Hon’ble Minister emphasized that PMIS is not restricted only to a candidate’s academic qualification. She said the scheme enables youth to pursue internship opportunities in areas of interest, helping them gain hands-on training and professional learning in those fields. She also advised the interns to perform their work with focus and responsibility, noting that even small mistakes can have consequences for others, including end consumers, and may affect the company’s quality and reputation.
The event showcased remarkable stories of transformation of youth through PMIS.
One such story was that of Dhruv Gupta from Delhi, who is interning with NSE. Coming from an IT background, Dhruv had always aspired to gain exposure in the finance sector. Through this scheme, he received an opportunity to work in finance and hopes to build a career in the fintech sector by combining his technical knowledge with the financial skills gained during the internship.
Gupta sharing his experience said, “PMIS gave me the opportunity to step into the finance sector despite my IT background. This experience has helped me understand how technology and finance can come together, and I now wish to pursue a career in fintech.”
Another inspiring story was that of Naina from Uttar Pradesh, who received an opportunity to intern with Alkem in Daman. Although the opportunity required her to move far from home to a new city, Naina was determined to gain new experience, with her family supporting her throughout the journey. After successfully completing her internship, she was offered a full-time role at Alkem, marking the beginning of a new professional chapter in her life. She said that, “Moving away from home was a big step, but my father encouraged me to take this opportunity. PMIS

articles.title: Ministry of Corporate Affairs hosts the PMIS Industry Awards in New Delhi to honour leading partner companies for creating meaningful internship opportunities for youth under the Prime Minister Internship Scheme
articles.full_content:
PMIS interns also to participate in the Independence Day celebrations in New Delhi
As part of the Independence Day celebrations, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA), Government of India, organized the PMIS Industry Awards on August 14, 2026, in New Delhi to recognize the contribution of partner companies in the successful implementation of the Prime Minister Internship Scheme (PMIS) during its pilot phase.
The event was chaired by the Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, and was attended by senior officials of the Ministry, representatives from leading industry partners, and more than 100 current and former PMIS interns from across the country.
The awards celebrated organizations that have demonstrated exceptional commitment to nurturing young talent, creating high-quality internship opportunities, adopting effective internship management practices, and supporting the Government’s vision of building a future-ready workforce. Mahindra & Mahindra Limited was recognized as the Overall Industry Champion for its leadership and exemplary contribution to promoting internships and youth engagement under PMIS.
Industry representatives shared positive experiences from their participation in the Scheme and highlighted the value created for both organizations and interns. A representative from Mahindra & Mahindra Limited said, “Today, we have crossed the milestone of welcoming 1,000 interns across the Mahindra Group.
This is nearly five times the number of interns who joined us in Round II and reflects how the PM Internship Scheme has evolved from a budding initiative into a programme operating at scale.” IBM also highlighted the value that interns bring to companies, noting that their fresh perspectives, curiosity, and willingness to learn have enriched teams, supported innovation, and reinforced the importance of developing future-ready, industry-relevant skills.
A representative from Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories shared an inspiring example of how PMIS is helping interns build future pathways, recalling that an intern used the PMIS internship certificate to secure admission to a pharmaceutical course at Long Island University, Brooklyn. The example reflected the Scheme’s potential not only to provide workplace exposure but also to support higher education and long-term career growth.
Western Coalfields Limited expressed appreciation for the Scheme, noting that PMIS helped the organization attract young talent to collieries in rural and semi-urban areas of Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, where sourcing interns had traditionally been challenging. The experience demonstrated the Scheme’s ability to connect youth with opportunities beyond major urban centres while addressing manpower requirements across diverse industry locations .
